content:
Indian security forces killed Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Mohammad Lateef Bhat in an encounter in south Kashmir's Kulgam district early on Wednesday, in an operation the government described as eliminating the last known active local militant of the group in the Kashmir Valley.

Bhat was killed after an eight-day cordon and search operation in Zangalpora village in the Devsar area of Kulgam, where he had taken shelter inside a mosque during a chase by security forces. Kashmir Police said the body of one militant, along with a weapon, had been recovered from the encounter site, and identified him as Mohammad Lateef Bhat, a resident of Khrewan village in Kulgam. Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced the killing on social media, saluting what he called the coordinated efforts of the Jammu and Kashmir Police, the Indian Army, the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and intelligence agencies.

"With the coordinated efforts of JKP, Indian Army, CRPF and intelligence agencies, Lashkar's last known active local terrorist in the valley, Lateef Bhat, was neutralised in an operation in Kulgam in the early morning hours today," Shah wrote. He added that one of Bhat's associates, Umar Nisar, had also been killed in Kulgam the day before, and that the operation "was marked by a very high level of synergy".

The operation began after an attack on a CRPF party in the Akhran area near Nowpora in Kulgam on November 11, in which three personnel were injured. According to [The Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/in-just-one-week-how-security-forces-avenged-attack-on-crpf-personnel-in-kulgam/articleshow/135949647.cms), security forces launched an extensive search involving CCTV footage and repeated intelligence inputs, and Bhat was eventually trapped inside the mosque in Zangalpora. He refused to surrender despite repeated appeals, and opened fire on the forces at around 3:45am, triggering the gunfight in which he was killed. Police said the forces had exercised restraint to avoid damaging the religious structure while the standoff continued.

Bhat, 22, had joined Lashkar-e-Taiba exactly a year ago, on November 18, 2025, according to police officials cited by [The Wire](https://thewire.in/security/let-commander-lateef-bhat-killed-in-kulgam-encounter), and his family had reported him missing that month. Police listed him as the lone surviving active local commander of the group in Kashmir, and accused him of involvement in the November 11 attack on the CRPF party as well as other attacks in south Kashmir. His associate Umar Nisar Dar was killed in a gunfight near the Laroo bypass in Kulgam shortly before Bhat's death, in a second encounter during the same sweep.

The claim that Bhat was the last active local militant carries real significance if it holds. Security officials believe the Valley may now have no listed active local terrorist, a milestone Indian authorities have not been able to claim before. But the description comes with an important qualification: it refers to local recruits listed by the police, not to foreign fighters, and the assessment rests on the security forces' own records rather than on independent verification. Lashkar-e-Taiba, the Pakistan-based group Bhat belonged to, is designated a terrorist organisation by India, the United States and the United Nations, and has been blamed for some of the deadliest attacks in India, including the 2008 Mumbai attacks.

The killing comes amid intensified counter-terrorism operations across south Kashmir following the November 11 attack, with security forces conducting repeated cordon and search operations in Kulgam and neighbouring districts. Local recruitment into militant groups has fallen sharply in recent years, according to Indian officials, and the police have increasingly described the remaining local cadres as a small, shrinking pool. Whether the Valley stays free of active local militants will depend on whether that trend continues, and on whether the groups can still recruit or infiltrate fighters from across the Line of Control.

The operation was the second counter-terrorism success to make headlines this week, after authorities in North Macedonia said they had foiled an Iran-linked assassination plot targeting Israeli interests in Greece, as [Global Wire reported](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/ar/articles/north-macedonia-foils-iran-linked-assassination-plot-greece-november-2026). For New Delhi, the Kulgam operation is being presented as the closing of a chapter: the end of an eight-day hunt, the avenging of an attack on its paramilitary forces, and, in the government's telling, the removal of the last local commander of one of Kashmir's most active militant groups. The test of that claim will come in the months ahead, in whether any new local name appears on the police list.
summary: Indian security forces killed Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Mohammad Lateef Bhat in an encounter in Kulgam district on Wednesday after an eight-day search, in an operation the government described as eliminating the last known active local militant of the group in the Kashmir Valley.
title: India kills Lashkar commander Lateef Bhat in Kulgam, calling him Kashmir's last active local militant
